source_cards.title: Neural-Driven Multi-Band Processing for Automatic Equalization and Style Transfer
key_findings: Parameters are fixed within each 3 s or 6 s chunk.
No explicit crossover or band splitting is used; six PEQs and associated compressors are applied sequentially to full-band audio.
MUSDB18 stems are converted to mono and already contain unknown professional processing.
PEQ plus single-band DRC captured most MOS benefit and exceeded NDMP on several objective style-transfer metrics.
Claims of consistent objective superiority are not supported by the complete metric table.
limitations: No released NDMP implementation was identified in the paper.
Audio-example link was not resolvable from the read source.
The transient-preservation metric direction is insufficiently documented and discussed inconsistently.
Mono processed stems do not validate stereo or raw multitrack rock mixing.

source_cards.title: Listener Preferences for Alternative Dynamic-Range-Compressed Audio Configurations
source_cards.publication: Journal of the Audio Engineering Society 65(7/8), 540-551

study_design.stimulus: one unknown 10 s mono popular-music excerpt with eight raw tracks
study_design.level_matching: final RMS normalization -15 dBFS; mean -17.68 LUFS SD 0.09

key_findings: Compression was preferred more often than chance and limiting less often when pooled across other variables.
Track processing was preferred more often and full-sum processing less often when pooled across other variables.
Heavy full-sum limiting was especially disfavored.
Magnitude alone was marginal, and heavy track compression was among preferred interactions; the result is not simply less compression is better.
limitations: One 10 s mono excerpt and one processor.
Common 0.5 ms attack and 5 ms release were not optimized per source or topology.
Generalization to modern stereo rock or metal was not tested.

knowledge_cards.claim: Architecture labels require signal-path and probe verification; sequential full-band stages are not crossover multiband processing.
Fixed parameters per 3/6 s chunk are segment-conditioned, not time-varying within the chunk.
Every exposed DRC parameter needs an independent sensitivity/null test before it is treated as editable or interpretable.
A simpler PEQ plus single-band DRC baseline can retain most subjective benefit and win some objective targets.
Loudness, spectral alignment, crest, transient behavior, phase and preference must remain separate outputs when metrics disagree.
Processed mono stems cannot validate stereo, multi-mic phase, bleed or raw-track rock-mixing decisions.
At subgroup/full-sum points, peaks in one element can control gain applied to other elements; event-aligned cross-triggering is a diagnostic target.
Campbell et al. supports testing DRC placement and caution with heavy full-sum limiting, not universal genre settings.

rule_candidates.when_apply: processor claims multiband or per-band dynamics
rule_candidates.instrument_section: any source or bus; section-specific evaluation
rule_candidates.change: run in-band and out-of-band probes before accepting the topology label
rule_candidates.proposed_range: at least one in-band and one out-of-band probe per claimed band
rule_candidates.success: localized repeatable response on synthetic and music probes
rule_candidates.cancel: documented full-band topology or leakage disproves isolation

rule_candidates.when_apply: DRC parameter becomes a trainable or interpretable control
rule_candidates.change: one-control sweep with fixed other controls; compare GR and null
rule_candidates.success: independent predictable attack and recovery changes
rule_candidates.cancel: outputs or GR are unchanged or effect contradicts label

rule_candidates.when_apply: learned multistage or multiband dynamics is proposed
rule_candidates.change: compare no-processing, level-only, PEQ, PEQ+single-band DRC and complex system at matched loudness
rule_candidates.proposed_range: match audible processing depth rather than copy training ranges
rule_candidates.success: complex system wins a preregistered musical target without harming protected qualities
rule_candidates.cancel: simple baseline is equal or better

rule_candidates.when_apply: reference matching or DRC targets transient-rich material

rule_candidates.proposed_range: onset and tempo conditioned windows; no universal milliseconds claimed
rule_candidates.success: loudness-matched blind test preserves attack role and body without excess pumping
rule_candidates.cancel: metric improves while punch/body preference worsens

rule_candidates.when_apply: bus DRC audibly moves unrelated instruments after kick/snare peaks

rule_candidates.change: log event-aligned GR and compare local, track, subgroup and full-sum processing
rule_candidates.proposed_range: tempo/envelope matched; Campbell 0.5/5 ms and thresholds explicitly forbidden as presets
rule_candidates.success: desired density without unintended attenuation of neighboring roles

rule_candidates.instrument_section: verse, chorus and dense fill or solo; role-aware

rule_candidates.success: Dmitry preference is stable and protected qualities pass

handoff: Do not trust multiband labels without band-isolation probes. Fixed segment-level parameters are not time-varying within a segment. Preserve no-processing, level-only and PEQ+single-band baselines. For bus compression measure which source triggers GR and which neighboring roles are attenuated. Training ranges and one-excerpt listening-test settings are not rock presets.
